q1.answer: ADR007 decided that any fetch or XMLHttpRequest in tests should be mocked with msw's express-style route handlers (as react-testing-library recommends) instead of each test mocking fetch its own way; the ADR's example is exactly this server.use(http.get(...)) pattern from CatalogClient.test.ts. Mocking at the network layer also exercises the client's real URL building and response handling.

q2.answer: ADR014, which supersedes ADR013's node-fetch recommendation, says frontend plugins and packages should prefer fetchApiRef, and that clients should accept an injected fetch so callers can add auth or other information and track metrics, rather than depending on third-party fetch packages. Notifications is a frontend plugin, so it gets fetchApi from fetchApiRef.

q3.answer: ADR010 makes Luxon Backstage's standard date library for formatting (e.g. 'a day ago') and calculations the native Date can't easily do; Moment.js was rejected for large bundle size, mutable state and being sunset, and a single library keeps bundles small and avoids learning several APIs. Luxon is immutable and Intl-based, and toRelative() gives the relative text directly.

q4.answer: ADR006 says React.FC and React.SFC should be avoided in new code because they implicitly add children props and don't support generic types on children (the reason Facebook removed React.FC from the create-react-app TypeScript template); components type their props argument directly instead.

q5.answer: ADR004 requires every exported symbol to be traceable through index files down to src/index.ts, with each index re-exporting only from its immediate children and only index files doing re-exports, so you can tell whether a symbol is public by walking index files toward the root. Reaching into deeper files from src/index.ts would break that rule and make module boundaries unpredictable.
